claim_findings.passage: Management describes a mild but broad-based loosening in competitors' credit underwriting standards
claim_findings.evidence: In seg-0091 Dimon says 'it's across several spectrum' but then immediately adds 'and this is not across the board, by the way. It's more some players than others.' The word 'broad-based' reads naturally as broad across lenders, which is the opposite of what he said. The claim_text does preserve the qualifier in its second half, and 'broad' is defensible as meaning broad across types of loosening, so the reading is recoverable but the wording invites the wrong one.
claim_findings.recommendation: Reword claim_text to say the loosening spans several dimensions of underwriting but is concentrated in some lenders rather than industry-wide, so the word 'broad' cannot be read as applying to lenders.

claim_findings.evidence: The claim_text asserts 'net income of $3.3 billion on revenue of $11.3 billion, up 5% year-on-year', but the claim's own quote contains only the net income figure. The revenue figure and the 5% growth rate are real and appear in web-002, but they sit in claim-041's quote, not this one. The existing note in .agents/memory/extractor-lessons.md ('Keep each claim's quote self-sufficient') already covers this pattern, so it is a repeat rather than a new failure mode.
claim_findings.recommendation: Either extend claim-040's quote to the full 'Consumer Banking • Net income of $3.3 billion • Revenue of $11.3 billion, up 5%' bullet, or trim claim_text to the net income figure alone and leave the revenue statement to claim-041.

claim_findings.evidence: The claim_text was corrected this round to say the $40 billion is excess capital that management distinguishes from buying back stock, which seg-0079 fully supports ('if we think we can deploy, it's very different than buying back stock'). outlook_findings.passage: which is the kind of dynamic management explicitly says produces uneven outlier losses in the next credit cycle rather than a smooth downturn [claim-022]
outlook_findings.evidence: Section 7 attributes this statement to management and cites claim-022. Neither claim-022's quote nor its claim_text says anything about the next credit cycle or about outlier losses. The statement is in fact true of the transcript: later in seg-0091 Dimon says 'when there's a credit cycle, and there will be a credit cycle, how will everybody perform. And I don't think it's going to be like a bell curve of performance. I think there'll be some outliers out there.' But that sentence was never extracted into any claim, so the citation resolves to a topically adjacent claim that does not establish the sentence it is attached to. A reader auditing the brief through claim-022 would not find the assertion.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Extract the bell-curve/outliers sentence from seg-0091 as its own claim and cite that alongside claim-022, or drop the phrase 'management explicitly says' and the outlier-loss characterization from section 7.

outlook_findings.passage: and the broader risk-on market backdrop management describes [claim-012] persists longer than Dimon's own "getting close to as good as it gets" framing implies [claim-046]

The claim-046 half of the sentence is correctly grounded: seg-0040 contains that quote verbatim, and it is Dimon answering an analyst who asked 'Is this as good as it gets?'.

outlook_findings.passage: deposit betas continuing to outperform JPMorgan's model as they have so far this cycle [claim-021]
outlook_findings.evidence: claim-021 is forward-looking. It records management's stress-testing point that rate paid on deposits could accelerate beyond what earnings-at-risk models assume in a regime change. It says nothing about betas having outperformed to date. That trailing factual clause traces to the analyst's question in seg-0040 ('betas, which you alluded to earlier have been better than expected so far'), which was not extracted as a claim. The forward-looking half of the indicator is properly supported; only the backward-looking clause is not.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Drop 'as they have so far this cycle', or extract management's own statement on realized deposit betas as a claim and cite it.

outlook_findings.passage: Management still frames roughly $40 billion as excess capital -- explicitly distinct from buyback capacity -- that it now believes it can deploy organically over time, against a stated target of deploying capital at a 17% return [claim-028][claim-029]
outlook_findings.evidence: The characterization is correct and seg-0079 supports it fully. The completeness gap is that section 3 discusses capital deployment without anywhere in the brief surfacing the two validated capital claims that show capital being consumed this quarter: claim-005 (CET1 down 20 basis points to 14.1%) and claim-006 (standardized risk-weighted assets up about $103 billion). outlook_findings.recommendation: Add a sentence in section 3 or section 8 noting the quarter's CET1 decline and risk-weighted-asset growth, citing claim-005 and claim-006, so the capital-deployment discussion carries the offsetting capital consumption.

summary: No blocking findings. The high-severity problem from the previous round is genuinely fixed rather than merely narrated as fixed: web-003 was opened and is a clean Wells Fargo press release matching claim-044 and claim-045 verbatim, the second Wells Fargo source (web-008) really is an unlabelled chart deck exactly as section 9 now describes, and both Wells Fargo results are cited in the brief. The $40 billion capital point in claim-028 and section 3 now matches what Dimon actually said in seg-0079, where he explicitly separates deploying capital from buying back stock. Section 5 now carries a counterevidence paragraph setting Citigroup's 45% and Bank of America's 70% Equities gains against management's own not-repeatable framing, and the 'as good as it gets' quotation is grounded in claim-046. One medium finding remains: section 7 attributes to management a statement about uneven outlier losses in the next credit cycle and cites claim-022, which contains no such statement. The sentence is true of the transcript, but the underlying words in seg-0069's neighbouring segment were never extracted, so the citation resolves to an adjacent claim that does not establish it. Five low findings follow, covering a miscount of peer sources in section 9, a 'risk-on' gloss on management's 'highly dynamic' wording, an unsupported trailing clause about realized deposit betas, a stale values key on claim-028, and the brief never surfacing the quarter's CET1 decline and risk-weighted-asset growth while discussing capital deployment. Deterministic gates all passed with 46 claims and zero issues, the injection scan was clean, period labelling is unambiguous and consistent with the SEC half-year facts, temporal integrity holds across all cited evidence, and the prose is appropriately bank-specific throughout.
proposed_lessons: When the brief attributes a statement to management, the cited claim must itself contain that statement; extract a new claim for it rather than citing a topically adjacent claim from the same part of the call.
